scope: Selected institutional and conflict milestones, not an exhaustive military history. Wikipedia-derived entries are secondary and require corroboration.

items.title: Partition and service division
items.summary: At independence, armed forces, ships, aircraft and formations were divided between India and Pakistan. The new services inherited distinct starting inventories.

items.title: First India–Pakistan war
items.summary: The armed forces fought the first Kashmir conflict after independence; the event shaped early force organization and operational experience.

items.title: Operation Polo
items.summary: Indian forces entered Hyderabad in September 1948; the state was integrated into the Indian Union.

items.title: First Indian Army Commander-in-Chief
items.summary: K. M. Cariappa became the first Indian Commander-in-Chief of the Army; 15 January is observed as Army Day.

items.title: Republic and national service identities
items.summary: On becoming a republic, colonial-era service titles and symbols were progressively replaced by Indian national insignia.

items.title: First Indian Air Chief
items.summary: Subroto Mukherjee became the first Indian Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Air Force.

items.title: Chiefs of Staff designation
items.summary: Legislation changed the service chiefs’ designation from Commander-in-Chief to Chief of Staff.

items.title: First Indian Chief of Naval Staff
items.summary: The last British naval chief was succeeded by an Indian officer, according to the linked historical account.

items.title: Goa / Operation Vijay
items.summary: Army, Navy and Air Force took part in the operation that ended Portuguese rule in Goa.

items.title: Sino-Indian War
items.summary: The conflict with China prompted major reassessment of high-altitude readiness, logistics and force posture.

items.title: India–Pakistan War
items.summary: A major interstate conflict involving the armed forces; included as historical context, not a detailed operational account.

items.title: India–Pakistan War and Bangladesh liberation
items.summary: All three services participated in the war that led to the creation of Bangladesh.

items.title: Operation Meghdoot
items.summary: Indian forces established positions on the Siachen Glacier and Saltoro Ridge; this began a continuing high-altitude deployment.

items.title: Indian Peace Keeping Force in Sri Lanka
items.summary: IPKF deployed under the Indo–Sri Lanka Accord; the experience informed later counter-insurgency and joint operations discussions.

items.title: Kargil conflict
items.summary: The conflict underscored requirements in surveillance, high-altitude logistics, precision fires and joint coordination.

items.title: Defence Intelligence Agency established
items.summary: Post-Kargil reforms led to the establishment of the Defence Intelligence Agency, which became operational in 2002.

items.title: Department of Military Affairs created
items.summary: The Ministry of Defence annual report records creation of the Department of Military Affairs in 2019 to promote jointness and resource coordination.

items.title: Chief of Defence Staff and jointness reforms
items.summary: The CDS and Department of Military Affairs framework became a visible institutional modernization focus; verify individual dates against official releases.

items.title: Agnipath recruitment scheme introduced
items.summary: A major personnel policy change altered short-service recruitment pathways for the Army, Navy and Air Force.

items.title: Operation Sindoor and contemporary force posture
items.summary: Recent event named in the current Wikipedia overview; expand only alongside official statements and reputable independent reporting.
